decisions.decision: Join coverage lines to requirements by heading through the shared requirement key, and by FR id when one is present
decisions.why: Cards key on the heading and this repo s living specs carry no ids, so an id-only join leaves every real card blank
decisions.rejected: Reusing the header s id-only count

decisions.decision: Label is N tests, or F/N tests when some named test files are missing; no entry when no test is named
decisions.why: The living spec rule requires a missing test to read differently from an unmapped requirement
decisions.rejected: A bare count, and checking test names inside files

decisions.decision: Ride the existing livingHealthResolved message with one optional field
decisions.why: The message contract is declared once and drift and new marks already travel this way

decisions.decision: Webview clears the map when the spec path on screen changes
decisions.why: The provider skips the health message when nothing resolved, so stale labels would survive a capability switch
decisions.rejected: Always posting a health message, which changes behaviour for capabilities with no coverage

decisions.decision: Extension builds the label from integers and fixed words
decisions.why: The card writes it into an attribute through an escape that does not cover quotes
decisions.rejected: Rewriting the card renderer to use DOM APIs

decisions.decision: A coverage line goes to the longest requirement heading it names
decisions.why: A requirement called Adds would otherwise claim a line written for Adds an item

decisions.decision: Join by id only when the id is in the requirement heading
decisions.why: Ids in a body belong to bullets under a grouping heading, which has no card of its own
decisions.rejected: Ids found anywhere in the requirement body, as the plan first said

decisions.decision: Test paths are read token by token, and headings are searched outside those paths and outside test selectors
decisions.why: Two review rounds showed a single path regex cut paths with route-group parens, took spec documents for tests, and let a heading or id inside a path claim the line
decisions.rejected: The single TEST_PATH_RE from the first pass

decisions.decision: A coverage line labels every requirement it names, and only the id a heading opens with is its own
decisions.why: One line often lists several ids, and a heading that mentions another id must not take or cancel its label

decisions.decision: No extra provider state to clear labels
decisions.why: Every living update reloads the webview, which resets them; the set added after review round one was dead code and was removed in round two
decisions.rejected: A per-spec set that forces an empty health message
